solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novel prize I malign without hesitation

parts.note: a prize is a treasure, something greatly valued

indicators.note: ER is the written sound of a hesitation, so it is taken out of the verb

parts.note: to malign someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a book that won an award, without pausing to hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' removes ER from SLANDER, leaving SLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate adventure is a famous novel.

clue.text: Desire short-sleeved top, when moving south

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving south means one letter of the garment slides further down the column

parts.note: a short-sleeved top is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Wanting a T-shirt when heading off to a warmer climate.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of T-SHIRT moves down three places, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a craving or longing, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Bug creating rage around female group

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit around the group's abbreviation
creating in the sense of making a fuss means the letters of rage are thrown about

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: An insect has got a women's club in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is the definition, read as the insect. 'creating' (making a fuss) shuffles the letters to EARG; the Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is an insect, and bug is a loose everyday word for any insect.

clue.text: Sense this rising will stifle government

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the reversed word closes round the abbreviation
in a down clue, rising means the word this is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A feeling that something about to grow will choke the administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns THIS into SIHT; 'will stifle' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, alongside hearing, touch, taste and smell.

clue.text: Beyond river, one struggles to behead snake

indicators.note: beyond means the following letters come after the river's abbreviation

parts.note: R is the usual map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: beheading removes the opening letter of the fighter's word

parts.note: one who struggles or fights on is a battler

explanation.surface: Across the water, a fighter tries to cut the head off a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to behead' drops the B of BATTLER, leaving ATTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is an informal American name for the rattlesnake.

clue.text: See 1
Speak now to vacant upstart after one refuse area's overturned

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the reversed part
overturned means the numeral and the dumps are written in reverse order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a refuse area is a tip, a rubbish dump; the plural tips is read here
taken as written

indicators.note: vacant means the word upstart is emptied of its inside letters, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Telling an empty-headed young pretender to talk, after a rubbish dump is flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses I TIPS to SPITI; 'vacant' empties UPSTART to UT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit it out is an idiom urging a hesitant person to say what they mean.

clue.text: Everyone joined Tracey right away handling stray animal

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: handling means manipulating, so the remaining letters are reworked
right away means the R for right is taken out of the name

explanation.surface: Everyone teamed up with Tracey, who at once took charge of a stray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' drops R from TRACEY to leave TACEY; 'handling' rearranges that to EYCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray urban cat that roams back streets.

clue.text: Neglected food shop keeps on casual types primarily

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the shop's word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop
re means on or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: primarily means the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A neglected delicatessen still serves people dressed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' makes DERELI; 're' meaning 'on' is the business-letter sense, as in 're your enquiry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict describes something abandoned and left to decay, so neglected.

clue.text: Cook in boiling water

indicators.note: in places the falsifying word inside the angry word

parts.note: someone boiling with rage is irate
to cook the books is to rig or falsify them

explanation.surface: A simple kitchen instruction to cook something in boiling water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is not about kitchens: it means rig, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land or crops with water, often through channels.

clue.text: One directs packet to central Somerset

parts.note: a packet is a large sum of money, and a till is where shop money is kept

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the county name

explanation.surface: A man sending a parcel to the heart of Somerset, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes the middle pair ER from the eight letters of SOMERSET, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the handle a sailor uses to steer, so it directs a boat.

clue.text: Given fish, have a bone to pick

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of ponds and rivers, prized by anglers
to have a grievance and complain about it, especially pettily

explanation.surface: Handed a fish, someone has a complaint about the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Carp is both a common freshwater fish and a verb meaning to grumble or nag.

clue.text: A bit hurt during wild antics

indicators.note: during means the sick word comes in the middle of the shuffled letters
wild means the letters of antics are thrown into disorder

parts.note: hurt can mean ill or poorly

explanation.surface: Someone got a little injured during some reckless horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' gives SCINTA, which 'during' splits before its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, as in not a scintilla of evidence.

clue.text: Some fully discussed retrospective poem

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the run of letters is read backwards
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A poem looking back on matters that were thoroughly talked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes LLYDI from fuLLY DIscussed; 'retrospective' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: Match beginning in party atmosphere

indicators.note: beginning in means the first letter of the word party

parts.note: air is the atmosphere or the feel of a place

explanation.surface: A romance starting in the buzz of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two matching things, and to match is to pair up.

clue.text: High-flyer's under-par performance?

definitions.meaning: a huge seabird that glides for long distances over oceans
in golf, a score of three strokes under par on one hole

explanation.surface: A star achiever's disappointing showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-par' reads as substandard, but in golf under par is good.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seabird gives its name to the golf score three under par.

clue.text: Dull experts reflecting intelligence

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the agency's letters are reversed

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: Boring specialists thinking about intelligence matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns CIA into AIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means ordinary and unimaginative, lacking poetry or excitement.

clue.text: Did train drive away, guided around cape

indicators.note: around means the shooing word goes round the cape's letter

parts.note: shoo is what you say to drive away an animal
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
guided means led

explanation.surface: A locomotive pulled away, steered round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside SHOO to give SCHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooled means taught or trained, the past tense of school as a verb.

clue.text: A Parisian attracted by sweet cream

indicators.note: attracted by means the French word is drawn to and placed after the pudding

parts.note: afters is British slang for a dessert or sweet course
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman drawn to a sugary cream cake.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftersun is a soothing lotion applied to skin after sunbathing.

clue.text: Bachelor in panic, going on about where to drink

indicators.note: going on means following, so the scared word comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: in places the bachelor's letter inside the panic word

parts.note: panic is fear
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees

explanation.surface: A single man is in a state, ranting about where to get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside FEAR to give FEBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe bar is a place serving coffee and alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Seasoned beef not the starter

indicators.note: not the starter means the first letter is dropped from the grumble word

parts.note: a beef is a complaint or gripe

explanation.surface: Spiced beef, but no appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is a complaint, not meat; 'not the starter' drops the G of GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe and seasoned both describe matured cheese or wood, or an aged person.

clue.text: Fairy story writer's wanting first and last to teach

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as the writer, so writer's means my

indicators.note: first and last means the outside letters of the word teach

explanation.surface: An author of fairy tales lacking anything to teach.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the writer, so writer's is MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, and a fairy story is any invented or untrue tale.

clue.text: One makes music graduates entertain outer circle

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so the degrees enclose the edge

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
the rim is the outer circle of a wheel or bowl

explanation.surface: Someone producing music for graduates hosting an exclusive circle.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'graduates', supplies both degrees; 'entertain' sets the edge between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a wooden percussion instrument, so it is something that makes music.

clue.text: Modern artist seen among private stars

indicators.note: seen among means the artist sits inside the soldier's letters

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
Tracey Emin is a British contemporary artist

explanation.surface: A contemporary artist spotted among celebrities in a private setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a constellation, a group of stars known as the Twins.

clue.text: Force opening of safety lock

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of safety

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Forcing open a safety catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is force or pressure applied to something, as in engineering.

clue.text: Public old green in Provence

parts.note: vert is French for green, Provence being a French region

explanation.surface: An old village green somewhere in the south of France open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, so in public view rather than hidden.

clue.text: Appropriate training drained Robert in medical department

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training

indicators.note: drained means the inside letters of the name are emptied out

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Fitting that an exhausted Robert ends up in a hospital unit after exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' empties ROBERT to RT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant or apt to the matter in hand.

clue.text: At home, regularly regret being immobile

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of regret, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Staying in and constantly regretting being unable to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means lacking the ability or power to move, motionless.

clue.text: City's the centrepiece for A-list bigwig on the comeback

indicators.note: the centrepiece means the middle letters of A-list, without its ends
on the comeback means the toff's word is read backwards

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or important person, a bigwig

explanation.surface: A city is the focal point for a celebrity big shot making a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centrepiece for' takes LIS from A-LIST; 'on the comeback' turns NOB into BON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: Stupid one putting insects back among decoration

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: among places the reversed bugs inside the honour's letters

parts.note: an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: back means the bugs' word is read in reverse

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A fool sticks insects into a piece of ornamentation backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives ECIL, which 'among' sets inside the honour after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecile, as an adjective, means foolish or idiotic.

clue.text: Bakery produce Prince, extremely adventurous, samples with tongue

parts.note: a tongue is a language, and Danish is the language of Denmark

indicators.note: extremely means the two outermost letters of adventurous

parts.note: to sample is to try, so samples means tries

explanation.surface: A bold prince tastes things using his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' means a language, not the organ; 'extremely' gives AS from ADVENTUROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish pastries are sweet flaky baked goods sold in bakeries.
